title: Protocol for Building Compartmental Models from Research Papers
description: Step-by-step guide for extracting epidemiological models from academic papers

steps.title: Initial Paper Reading
steps.description: Read paper abstract and introduction to identify disease and model type
actions: Read abstract to understand the research question
Read introduction to identify the disease being modeled
Identify model type (SEIR, SEIRS, SIR, etc.)
Note if paper mentions stratification, interventions, or special features
steps.output: Disease name, model type, special features mentioned

steps.title: Locate Model Description
steps.description: Find Methods section and look for "Mathematical Model" or "Model Structure"
actions: Navigate to Methods/Modeling section
Look for headings: "Mathematical Model", "Model Structure", "Compartmental Model"
Find model diagram (usually Figure 1 or Figure 2)
Locate equation list or model equations
steps.output: Model diagram reference, equation section location

steps.title: Extract Compartments
steps.description: Identify all compartments from diagram, equations, or text

sources.method: Look for boxes/circles representing population states
Each differential equation typically represents one compartment
Look for phrases like "The model includes compartments for..."

actions: List all compartment names
Note primary names (e.g., "Susceptible")
Note secondary names if present (e.g., "presymptomatic", "quarantined")
Record initial population values if given
steps.output: List of compartments with names and initial values

steps.title: Extract Flows
steps.description: Identify flows between compartments by reading equations

flow_types.example: dS/dt = -β*S*I/N → ContactFlow from S to E
characteristics: Rate depends on product of two populations

flow_types.example: dE/dt = ... - σ*E → RateFlow from E to I
characteristics: Rate is constant (not dependent on other compartments)
Positive term not from another compartment
Represents births, recruitment, or external input
May be optional for short-term models

flow_types.pattern: Terms with - (outflow not to another compartment)
characteristics: Negative term not going to another compartment
May be optional for short-term models

actions: Read each differential equation
Identify positive terms (inflows)
Identify negative terms (outflows)
Classify each term as ContactFlow, RateFlow, ExternalSource, or ExternalSink
Note the rate parameter or value for each flow
steps.output: List of flows with source, target, type, and rate

steps.title: Extract Parameters
steps.description: Find all parameter values from tables, text, or supplementary materials

sources.method: Most common location - look for parameter table
Look for phrases like "transmission rate β = 0.3"
sources.example: "We used a transmission rate of β = 0.3 per day"

sources.method: Check supplementary files for additional parameters
sources.note: Some papers put detailed parameter tables in supplements

sources.method: Parameters may cite values from previous studies
sources.action: Note the reference and try to locate original source

actions: Locate parameter table (usually Table 1)
Extract parameter name, symbol, value, unit, description
Check for uncertainty information (ranges, confidence intervals)
Note if parameter is constant, variable, or expression
Record source (table, text, supplementary, reference)
steps.output: List of parameters with values, units, and sources

steps.title: Extract Stratification
indicators: Check if parameters have subscripts (β_child, β_adult)
Look for separate equations for different groups
Check model diagram for multiple parallel compartments
actions: Search text for stratification keywords
Identify group categories (age, gender, risk, location)
List group values (e.g., "0-17", "18-64", "65+")
Note if parameters differ by stratum
Check if flows have stratum-specific rates
steps.note: Stratification is OPTIONAL - only extract if paper mentions it

steps.title: Record Initial Conditions
steps.description: Extract initial population values for each compartment
sources: Text: "We initialized with S(0) = X, I(0) = Y..."
Figure caption: Initial values in simulation description
actions: Find initial condition statement
Extract population value for each compartment
Calculate total population if not given
Note if initial conditions are stratified
steps.output: Initial population values for each compartment

steps.title: Document Missing Information
steps.description: Identify what information is missing or uncertain

examples: Parameter mentioned but no value given

actions: List all mentioned but undefined parameters
Note vague parameter descriptions
Record inaccessible references
Mark uncertain values with confidence level
Document assumptions made
